headline: DraftKings’ Predictions Bet Has Bulls Reeling From Sticker Shock
author: Peyton Forte

paragraphs.text: (Bloomberg) -- DraftKings Inc.'s plans to pour money into prediction markets is worrying Wall Street analysts who view the lack of regulatory clarity as a key risk, spurring a flood of downgrades for the stock.

The sports betting company is accelerating spending to acquire more customers for its prediction-market product, DraftKings Predictions. That growth is coming at the expense of its near-term profitability goals, with the company reducing its adjusted Ebitda forecast for this year by $575 million at the midpoint and initiating a 2027 outlook that disappointed.
The weak print forced at least five brokers, including JPMorgan, Wells Fargo and UBS, to drop their once bullish positions and step to the sidelines.

"What surprised us was the construction of the investment. It's the operating expenses related to startup costs around new states that were significantly higher, both this year and next, than our expectations," Wells Fargo analyst Trey Bowers, who cut DraftKings shares to equalweight from overweight Monday, said in an interview.

Shares of the Boston, Massachusetts-based firm tumbled 21% after it reported results postmarket Nov. 5, marking its worst single-day plunge in four years. The stock is down roughly 45% this year, on track for its worst annual performance since 2022.

After the recent wave of downgrades, the number of analysts with buy-equivalent ratings on the stock dropped to 26, the fewest since February 2024. Still, roughly two-thirds of the 40 DraftKings analysts tracked by Bloomberg rate the stock a buy. The average price target of $25.88 assumes a roughly 35% increase from where the shares closed Thursday.

The post-earnings rout came as DraftKings raised this year's prediction-market-related investments target to $675 million from about $250 million, both at the midpoint. For 2027, the expected size of the investment rises another $300 million from there.

Platforms like Kalshi and Polymarket are facing mounting legal challenges as states argue sports-related trades skirt local gaming rules and taxes. Analysts say the fight could end up in the hands of the US Supreme Court within the next two years, which could outlaw sports event contracts altogether.

"We've become more cautious on the digital gaming sector as the year progresses as the competitive intensity, in terms of sales and marketing spend as well as promotional spend, has continued to escalate against a backdrop of a very uncertain future for prediction-market-based sports-betting," Bowers said.

DraftKings' earnings estimates have started to come down as Wall Street resets its expectations. The average Ebitda estimate for the current fiscal year has slumped 64% over the past week, according to data compiled by Bloomberg. Expectations for 2027 profits are down almost 19% in that same period.

Some on Wall Street are sticking with their bullish calls despite the recent weakness. Bernstein analyst Ian Moore says the traction that DraftKings Predictions is gaining justifies the price tag, with the company noting that October consumer volumes were up nearly three times since July.
Here are other notable analyst calls and commentary this week:

• William Blair upgraded shares of Advanced Micro Devices Inc. to outperform from market perform, saying that the chipmaker's stock has a runway from here as its largest competitor, Nvidia, contends with the ouster of its CEO. Oppenheimer also upgraded shares of AMD to outperform from market perform this week.
• General Mills shares were cut to neutral from overweight at Piper Sandler, with analyst Michael Lavery saying that the risk of a dividend cut is too high.
• Capricor Therapeutics Inc. shares were raised to buy from hold at Jones ahead of its PDUFA date later in the month, which presents an "attractive catalyst" despite regulatory risk.
